name: white-model
title: Projection on white model
summary: A white massing model of a real place on a plinth in a dark room, and a projector painting data onto it one layer of light at a time.

look.ground: a dark room and a dark satin plinth; the model on a thin base plate, water as a darker inlay

palette.where: the white model in house light
one categorical accent for the exception (e.g. what was built before)
a sequential ramp for continuous data (blue to cyan to white)
warm sun on the model; shade projected deep blue

look.type: a light grotesk for the one figure (Inter Tight 200, 120-140 px), a sans for labels (Noto Sans SC), a monospace for years and coordinates (IBM Plex Mono); readout in the left third
look.texture: physical depth of field on close shots, bloom only on projection highlights, vignette, light grain
look.light: house light (one soft key) or projection added in the shader, facing-dependent with a soft throw edge; a real sun from the place's latitude and date
look.materials: matte white massing (roughness ~0.9) from real open building data; colour is never painted into the material

consistency: the model never changes, only the light on it; a colour returns only with the same meaning

motion.feel: slow continuous camera; light is the actor
moves: a wash spreading from the projector axis
buildings switching on one by one with a short flash
house lights cut fast (0.25 s) and return slowly (1 s)

pace.text: one readout per layer (index, figure, label, source); subtitles held at least max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s)

banned: invented buildings or a generated image of the place
more than two layer palettes on screen
a number not computed from the same data as the model
source: LemoLab's Projection on White Model style in lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar at 9eb7739; pace measured with analyze.py and events.py on its demo film "How a Flattened City Grew Back"
